title: Earliest music: bands on trucks
summary: Earliest music he remembers is the bands on trucks; recalls Rene, Guy Kelly and the clarinettist Georgie Boy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: I was going to ask something about the old-time banjo players. When you were a boy, even before you took up music or maybe even wanted to take up music, can you remember the very earliest music you ever heard? What kind of...
Well, during that time, the bands, they all used to be on the truck.
And I can remember Rene and they had Guy Kelly during that time. I think he was playing on the truck. I know Punch was around. Georgie Boy, because he stayed about three or four doors for me.
That's right. I know he lived over on Perdido Street. I met his wife there once. She still lived there.
He stayed about three or four doors for me.
How was he? How did he sound? I never got to hear him or meet him or...
Well, all I know, they could play that and it just sounded good to me then. Yeah, they all could play.
He used to have banjo or guitar in the wagon in those days?
Well, he used to have banjos. Banjos. Banjos. Banjos, yeah.

You know, Georgie Boy could talk to you in the clarinet, you know? He'd talk to his hands and his clarinet. Really? Yeah. He used to like it in his voice? We used to play with Guy at the Willow Inn. I remember he used to send John Kazmin nights that he had to work, you know, somewhere. Yeah.
